rows.name: Typed success / error / requirements
rows.measures: Errors and dependencies are tracked in the type of a program value; missing handling is a compile error.
rows.evidence: Effect<A,E=Never,R=HNil> is Send; typed HList R; compile-fail UI tests in crates/id_effect/tests/ui/.

checks.text: Program value type carries success, error and requirements parameters
Running with an unprovided dependency is a compile error (tested)
Infallible programs typed with an uninhabited error (Never/never/Nothing)
Mixing effects with different errors widens to a union without hand-written enums
Selective recovery (catchTag-style) removes only the handled error from the type
Providing a service removes it from the requirements type
Effects are lazy, re-runnable descriptions executed only by a runtime
Do-notation/generator syntax preserves all three type parameters

rows.name: Typed dependency injection
rows.measures: Declaring, providing, overriding and scoping services, checked before run time.
rows.evidence: crates/id_effect/src/layer.rs (succeed/effect/scoped/merge/provide_to/fresh/launch), caps!/need::<K>(); tests layer*.rs.

checks.text: Services declared as typed keys/interfaces, looked up by type
A missing service is a compile-time error
Modules/layers build services from other services (composable graph)
Shared instances memoised per graph, with an explicit fresh/transient opt-out
Scoped services: acquire on build, release on shutdown
Any service can be overridden with a test double without touching callers
Duplicate or conflicting providers are detected and rejected
Graph diagnostics: cycle detection and a renderable dependency graph

rows.name: Composition ergonomics
rows.measures: How short and readable everyday sequential/parallel code is.
rows.evidence: effect! sequential binds, ~(a,b) parallel join; retry/repeat need factories; pipe helpers removed.

checks.text: Sequential composition in native-looking syntax (async/await, do, generators)
Parallel fan-out of N tasks in one expression
One-call retry with a policy (no hand-written loop)
One-call timeout on any operation
Error conversion is implicit at bind sites (no map_err per call)
Typical service code needs no explicit type annotations
First-party lints/analyzers flag misuse in the IDE or CI
Official style/idiom guide for application code

notes.id_effect: 0.6.0 meets 4 of 8: no one-call timeout, generic runners need annotations, no first-party lints or idiom guide; v1 judged readability, which the checks do not see.

rows.name: Failure model (Cause / Exit)
rows.measures: Structured failure: expected errors, defects, interruption, composition and rendering.
rows.evidence: crates/id_effect/src/failure/{cause,exit}.rs; Die(Defect) keeps panic payload; tests/panic.rs.

checks.text: One Cause type separates expected failure, defect and interruption
Parallel and sequential cause composition kept (not only the first error)
Panics/exceptions captured as defects with the original payload
Any computation's full outcome observable as an Exit value
Human-readable rendering of composite causes
Handlers can recover from defects and interruption, not only typed errors
Failures carry stack or span traces
Cause queries and normalisation (failures/defects/interruptors, flatten)

notes.id_effect: The 0.6.0 kernel had no Cause or Exit: panics were not captured as defects, nothing recovered from defects or interruption, failures carried no traces (4 of 8).

rows.name: Resource safety (Scope / acquire-release)
rows.measures: Guaranteed release on success, failure and interruption; scoped lifetimes.
rows.evidence: kernel/resource.rs acquire_use_release/ensuring; finalizers run on interrupt; Layer::scoped.

checks.text: Bracket acquire/use/release; release runs once on success, failure, defect, interrupt
Release handler receives how the use phase ended
ensuring/finally combinator that also runs on interruption and panic
First-class Scope: add finalizers, close runs them once in LIFO order
Acquisition runs uninterruptibly (no leak between acquire and registration)
Scoped services: DI layer acquires on build and releases on app shutdown
Tasks can be bound to a scope; closing it interrupts and awaits them
Resource pool whose leases return automatically when the scope closes

notes.id_effect: 0.6.0 acquire_release ran release right after acquire and ensuring skipped drop and panic (4 of 8); no integration test, so level tested.

rows.evidence: uninterruptible/uninterruptible_mask/interruptible (kernel/resource.rs), parent interrupts children; tests/fibers.rs. No on_interrupt.

checks.text: Interrupt a running task from its handle and await its termination

Uninterruptible regions with restorable masks
Interrupting a parent interrupts its children

notes.id_effect: 0.6.0 cancellation was a manual CancellationToken/check_interrupt: no automatic interruption, masks, finalizers on interrupt or loser cleanup (3 of 8).

notes.otp: The checks reward structured-by-default children and virtual-time testing, which OTP lacks; v1 weighted process isolation.
